messages:
jordan: support ticket #4521 — customer reports missing audit events in their SIEM for window 2026-03-15 02:00-03:30 UTC. gaps in user.login and data.access. anyone own the SIEM connector for acme-enterprise?

maya: I can take a look. can you paste the org id and any forwarder id from the support bundle? any errors seen when they tail the forwarder logs?

jordan: org=acme-enterprise, forwarder id fd-7. Support says events are present in S3 but not indexed in their SIEM. they provided an s3 path: s3://redwood-audit/acme/2026-03-15/part-0003.gz

support_ana: we pulled that object — the file exists and contains events but several lines are missing tenant_id and sometimes principal fields. sample: 

```
{"event": "user.login", "user": "alice", "tenant_id": "acme-123"}
{"event": "user.login", "user": "bob"}  <-- tenant_id missing
{"event": "data.access", "principal": "svc-x", "tenant_id": "acme-123"}
```

sre_tom: if tenant_id is missing the SIEM mapping often drops the event. two hypotheses: (1) KMS rotation/re-encrypt step stripped metadata during re-encrypt, (2) forwarder flattening changed shape. @security-bot can you run schema-check on that prefix?

security-bot: schema-check queued for prefix /acme/2026-03-15/. result: 402 objects inspected, 3 distinct top-level shapes for login events: [ {user, tenant_id}, {user}, {actor, principal} ]. flagged objects: 78 with missing tenant_id. also flagged mismatched content-encoding header on 14 objects.

ops-oncall: noticed forwarder metrics show several HTTP 413 responses from customer's SIEM endpoint around 02:10 UTC for forwarder fd-7. batch size ~1.6MB. Splunk refused the batch which led to drops (no DLQ was configured for this org).

jordan: customer notes there was a KMS key rotation for that org at 2026-03-14 23:59 UTC. could a rotation have produced partially re-encrypted objects and stripped object-level metadata (x-amz-meta-tenant)? any decryption errors in forwarder logs?

maya: checking forwarder logs now — found repeated "decryption failed: key not found" for s3 object key acme/2026-03-15/part-0003.gz. Also seeing warnings around content-encoding: gzip not set consistently. repro steps from support bundle:

support_ana: repro we ran locally:

```bash
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit/acme/2026-03-15/part-0003.gz - | gunzip | head -n 5
# output shows lines where tenant_id missing
```

sre_tom: action plan proposed:
1) run an S3 scan to list objects for acme with missing tenant_id and dump keys (I'll provide a one-off s3-select query).
2) enqueue a replay job that reprocesses the raw objects via the legacy decrypt pipeline (which still handles rotated keys), writing reprocessed records to the forwarder input topic.
3) patch forwarder to tolerate missing tenant_id by enriching from object key (e.g., infer tenant from prefix) and make DLQ mandatory for orgs with SIEM connectors.

maya: I'm opening an incident PR and escalating to KMS team to verify rotation logs at 2026-03-14 23:59. @ops-oncall can you temporarily lower batch size and enable DLQ for acme-enterprise?

ops-oncall: done — batch max set to 256KB for fd-7 and retries increased to 5. DLQ enabled at s3://redwood-audit/dlq/acme/. also adjusted forwarder config to set content-encoding=gzip where missing for re-ingest.

jordan: noted. forwarding update to customer and asking for patience. any ETA on replay?

sre_tom: replay job queued; estimate ~3 hours to catch up ~60k events. I'll post progress samples and first re-ingested event IDs in this thread.

maya: thanks team :thumbsup:
